meta.title: Test your theory of change — Evens Foundation
meta.description: Enter your strategy and get historical evidence, causal mechanisms, and hard questions to test whether it holds up. Free tool by Evens Foundation.

mechanisms.heading: How this could work — the causal chain
assumptions.heading: Hidden assumptions this theory rests on

history.heading: Historical examples
workbook.heading: Workbook — stress-test your theory
workbook.intro: Answer the questions below in your own words. Your responses save automatically in this browser, so you can come back later or share them with your team.
related.heading: Explore related work in this area on the Civic Tech Field Guide
feedback.heading: How did it go?
feedback.lead: Tell us what worked, what surprised you, or what was off.
feedback.placeholder: e.g., I tested 'mentoring young people → reduced political polarization'. The historical examples brought up cases I hadn't considered, but the evidence-against section felt thin. The probing questions were the most useful part — they reframed how I'd pitch this to a funder.
feedback.emailLabel: Your email (optional — only if you'd like a reply)
feedback.thanks: Thanks — your feedback is on its way. We read every note.
feedback.empty: Please add a short message before sending.
feedback.badEmail: That email address does not look valid.
share.heading: Share this theory
share.warning: Heads up — assume this link could be discovered online. Don't share it if your action or change contains anything you'd rather keep private.
share.storageNote: Your workbook answers stay in this browser only — they're saved to local storage and are not included in the shared link. Only the original action and change travel with the URL.
